newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SURVIVES SCARE AT IMOLA.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SURVIVES SCARE AT IMOLA.

text.p: Defending world 500cc champion Michael Doohan survived a scare in Friday's practice for the San Marino Grand Prix and had to settle for provisional second place on the grid behind Spain's Carlos Checa.
Doohan lost control of his Honda on a left hand bend as he tried to pass a slower rider during his final lap of the afternoon qualifying session.
He careered off the track, sped down a grass verge for several seconds and appeared to be heading straight for a perimeter wall before he hauled the bike to the left and back onto the tarmac.
He completed the lap, constantly looking over his shoulder and shaking his head, and said afterwards he was reasonably happy with the session.

"In general the bike doesn't seem too bad," he said. "I had a bit of a moment when I had a coming together with another rider when I was going for a good time. Because I was getting a bit frustrated I turned on the gas rather aggressively and ran off the track.
"I'm pleased enough with my position after the first qualifying session. Tomorrow we'll continue to work on tyre selection for the race."

Doohan, bidding for his fourth consecutive world title and his seventh victory of the season, clocked one minute 49.755, 0.381 seconds slower than Checa, also on a Honda, who lapped Imola's recently remodified circuit in 1:49.374.
Doohan's fellow Australian Anthony Gobert was third on a Suzuki in 1:50.096 with Japan's Nobuatsu Aoki on a Honda fourth.
Checa, who finished second in last week's Dutch Grand Prix behind Doohan, said he feared a backlash from the Australian in Saturday's second qualifying session for Sunday's race.
"I don't want to be too excited about being on pole because we'll still have to fight for it tomorrow," he said.
"When I was in my flying lap I knew that Doohan was behind me but I carried on and, from what I've been told, he had a big moment.
"Nevertheless, I'm sure he'll try to beat me tomorrow but at least it seems that this fastest time secures me a front row start for Sunday."
In the 250cc and 125cc categories local heroes Max Biaggi and Valentino Rosi also had to settle for second best.
Biaggi was outpaced by 250cc championship leader Ralf Waldmann of Germany while Rossi, who tops the overall standings in the 125cc title race, lost out to Japan's Tomomi Manako.
